title: Can’t See the Forest for the Trees
chapter: Can’t See the Forest for the Trees
lines: Can’t See the Forest for the Trees begins with AI editing that weakened its argument.
The sentences remained plausible while urgency, uncertainty, and responsibility became harder to see.
It connects that experience with institutions that improve local details while losing the larger problem.
Its personal inquiry links technological progress with dependence, blind spots, and possible correction.
Readers are invited to examine a measured optimism that keeps difficult consequences in view.

title: An edit can lose the argument
chapter: An edit can lose the argument
lines: The author describes AI revisions that preserved plausibility while softening the point he needed expressed.
His concern was not simply whether individual sentences remained correct.
Urgency, doubt, and responsibility were part of what the text was trying to communicate.
That experience becomes an entry into a larger problem of apparently reasonable simplification.
A local improvement can make the whole account less faithful to what matters.

title: The larger picture has costs
lines: The inquiry moves from individual blind spots toward power, markets, attention, and institutional dependence.
A system can reward improvements that leave its wider consequences difficult to perceive.
The author also examines the limits of his own entrepreneurial and technological perspective.
This personal position gives the argument stakes without making it an established theory of everything.
The book keeps asking which connections disappear when each participant follows a narrower picture.

title: An optimism with responsibilities
lines: Begin with the author's editing experience before following its links to larger systems.
The later chapters consider AI, limits, and possibilities for intervention without promising a guaranteed rescue.
Optimism appears as a commitment to useful action while difficult consequences remain visible.
The book invites readers to question both technological enthusiasm and the comfort of resignation.
Read it for a personal inquiry into seeing more clearly and remaining responsible for what follows.
